question: Ondansetron is the antiemetic of choice for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) because it blocks 5-HT₃ receptors both in the gut and at the chemoreceptor trigger zone, preventing the vagal afferent signal that initiates vomiting.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Ondansetron's efficacy in CINV depends on blocking peripheral 5-HT₃ receptors on gut vagal afferents (the primary trigger site) and central 5-HT₃ receptors in the CTZ — a mechanism perfectly matched to chemotherapy's serotonin-releasing effect on enterochromaffin cells.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Ondansetron blocks 5-HT₃ receptors on vagal afferent nerve terminals in the gut (where serotonin is released from enterochromaffin cells in response to cytotoxic chemotherapy) and in the area postrema/CTZ, providing dual-site suppression of CINV.
